title: Islamic Tabular Calendar Astronomical Epoch
intro: This tabular Islamic lunar calendar uses the astronomical Thursday epoch, one day earlier than the Friday civil variant.
epoch: 1 Muharram AH 1 is JDN 1948439 (15 July 622 Julian).
structure: Odd months have 30 days, even months 29, except Dhu al-Hijjah (month 12), which has 30 days in leap years. A common year is 354 days and a leap year 355.
model: The leap test is positive remainder (11 × year + 14) modulo 30 below 11. Eleven leap years occur per 30-year cycle of 10631 days. The day coordinate is epoch - 1 + day + floor((59(month-1)+1)/2) + 354(year-1) + floor((3+11year)/30).
example: The same tabular year/month/day denotes one day earlier than in the Islamic Civil provider. Year 2 adds a day to Dhu al-Hijjah; Safar remains 29 days.
history: Tabular Hijri conventions allow calculation without a published lunar observation. The astronomical-epoch label identifies the starting coordinate, not an observed-moon algorithm.
limits: The arithmetic does not certify historical or local crescent sightings or an authority's religious calendar.
